claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified despite a known utility-arrears-assistance limitation because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and a 6% monitored rollout with rollback is acceptable if the limitation is explicitly disclosed in the model card.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case is excluded from rollout, the policy predicate could be satisfied.
If a reviewed and approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed segment exists, the policy predicate could be satisfied.
If the model-card limitation is explicitly documented in an approved record and certification policy allows certification with disclosure despite continued exposure, the verdict could improve.
Absent exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or proof that disclosure was actually completed and sufficient under policy, certification remains under-supported.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual approved model card or disclosure record showing the utility arrears assistance limitation is explicitly documented.
Provide the rollout gate or cohort definition proving the affected use case is excluded, if that is being claimed.
Provide a reviewed and approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses utility arrears assistance exposure, if one exists.
Provide the governing certification criterion showing whether explicit disclosure alone is enough to certify when a known segment-level weakness remains exposed.
specific_concerns: The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance; the actor summary says neither condition is met.
The affected utility arrears assistance segment remains exposed in the initial cohort, so rollout controls do not resolve the policy predicate.
There is no admissible evidence here that the required model-card disclosure has actually been written, reviewed, and approved; the packet argues for disclosure but does not evidence completion.
The actor relies in part on public guidance to justify certification posture, but policy compliance turns on the internal predicate in the policy text, not general monitoring principles alone.
unsupported_claims: That certification is currently supportable, rather than only conditionally supportable after documented disclosure is actually in place.
That public model-card guidance and monitoring principles are sufficient to bridge the gap created by continued exposure without exclusion or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that monitored rollout plus rollback makes the current action compliant by itself.
